title: The Card You Can Reach - and its clock
question: The approval gate expires after 120s with no countdown and renders inline, so it can arrive below the fold while the clock runs. Where should it live, and how does it show its time?

views.description: Measured: inline at MessageItem.tsx:524, no notion of time anywhere in the card, arrives below the fold behind the composer
Docked above the composer while pending - unmissable by construction; costs a reload seam
Stays inline, a jump chip chases you and CARRIES THE CLOCK - reuses shipped 015-C; costs a travel step
Panel hosts it beside the existing PendingAskCard 'Needs you' - consistency; costs the 52px collapsed rail

real_strings.card has no clock: ChatToolApprovalCard.tsx - only 120 in the file is ARG_VALUE_CHARS

honest_net_new: A countdown CANNOT be built client-side: ToolApprovalRequest carries no deadline and 120.0 lives only in tool_dispatcher.py. Inventing it in the client duplicates a server constant and will drift. The deadline must go on the wire.

fallback.why: B's jump chip keeps the card in the transcript, so it needs no reload seam at all.
fallback.re_open_trigger: Fires if a docked approval's decision CANNOT be rendered back into the transcript from persisted state at the quality SeamCard already achieves for ask_user - i.e. if the resolved card would leave a hole on reload, or would need machinery beyond a new SeamKind. Decide this at plan-phase, before the dock is built, not after.

note_from_sketch_223: A's reload seam is CHEAPER than it looked. Sketch 223's winner D deletes SeamCard's write_todos and workspace_write arms but KEEPS ask_user, because it is the only record a human decided anything. An approval decision is the same category, so the docked card resolves through the pattern that survives - a new SeamKind, not new machinery.
